title: Does miR-214 lower Atf4 directly? Choose the controls
summary: Adding an agomir lowers Atf4 protein, and three explanations could account for it. Choose which extra experiments to run, within your slots, so that the explanations can be told apart.

result.title: After wild-type agomir-214 is added to cells, Atf4 protein falls but Atf4 RNA does not.
result.detail: miR-214 is the suspected cause. Three explanations could account for the fall in protein.

hypotheses.name: miR-214 pairs with the Atf4 3' UTR and blocks its translation
Putting a large amount of any RNA into the cells lowers protein levels
miR-214 acts on something else, which then lowers Atf4

conditions.name: Add an unrelated negative-control RNA at the same dose
Add an agomir-214 with a few base changes
Luciferase reporter with the wild-type Atf4 3' UTR, plus agomir-214
Luciferase reporter with a mutated Atf4 3' UTR, plus agomir-214
Luciferase reporter with an unrelated 3' UTR, plus agomir-214
Repeat the first experiment with wild-type agomir-214

spec.lesson: An unrelated RNA shows whether any RNA would do it, and the reporter with the Atf4 3' UTR shows whether miR-214 acts through that site, which separates a direct effect from an indirect one. Repeating the experiment gives the same result whatever is true.
spec.note: The reporter sits under an unrelated promoter, so an indirect effect on Atf4 itself would not change it.
